sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.

sentences.zh: “来吧，让你看看如果不是书呆子，这事该怎么做。”

sentences.en: So on to programming news.
sentences.zh: 好了，进入编程新闻环节。

sentences.en: Yeah, speaking of exercising, let's exercise our processors with running CUDA natively on the CPU.
sentences.zh: 对，说到锻炼，让我们在 CPU 上原生运行 CUDA，以此来锻炼一下我们的处理器吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, so I know you've done this a little and I've done some of this, but there's, you know, the new, one of the new things that's come out recently is the programming,
sentences.zh: 对，我知道你对此略有涉猎，我也做过一些，不过最近出现的新事物之一就是关于编程的，

sentences.en: general purpose programming of graphics processing units.
sentences.zh: 图形处理单元的通用编程。

sentences.en: So the things that are in your computers, pretty much all the computers nowadays to some extent to run your graphics and, you know,
sentences.zh: 也就是你电脑里的那些芯片，基本上现在所有的电脑都在一定程度上配备了它们，用来运行你的图形，你知道的，

sentences.en: accelerate anything to doing with drawing to the screen with 3D rendering, like for games and all that's handled by these GPUs, which the basically come down to many cores, small,
sentences.zh: 加速任何与在屏幕上绘制 3D 渲染相关的内容，比如游戏等等，这些全部由这些 GPU 处理，它们基本上由许多核心组成，都是些小型、

sentences.en: lightweight processing cores that are able to do tons of tasks in parallel.
sentences.zh: 轻量级的处理核心，能够并行处理大量任务。

sentences.en: For instance, when you, you know, have to figure out where a triangle should show up on the screen,
sentences.zh: 举个例子，当你要计算一个三角形应该显示在屏幕的什么位置时，

sentences.en: there's maybe millions and millions of triangles on us in a given frame of a game.
sentences.zh: 在游戏给定的某一帧中，可能会有数以百万计的三角形。

sentences.en: And so you can do all of those calculations in parallel.
sentences.zh: 因此你可以并行执行所有这些计算。

sentences.en: And so these graphics processing units have gotten really, really good at doing things in parallel.
sentences.zh: 所以这些图形处理单元在并行处理任务方面变得非常非常强大。

sentences.en: And probably the most, so I don't know, I, so ATI and NVIDIA are the two big graphics processing people.
sentences.zh: 而且可能最，我不知道，我，ATI 和 NVIDIA 是两大图形处理巨头。

sentences.en: And so they each.
sentences.zh: 所以它们各自……

sentences.en: Well, ATI, ATI got bought by AMD.
sentences.zh: 哦对了，ATI 被 AMD 收购了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 原来如此。

sentences.en: But yeah.
sentences.zh: 不过是的。

sentences.en: So AMD and NVIDIA and Intel's now starting to do, well, both of them now are starting to even, Intel and AMD.
sentences.zh: 所以 AMD 和 NVIDIA，以及现在开始涉足的 Intel，好吧，现在这两家，Intel 和 AMD，

sentences.en: are starting to do interesting things with putting CPUs on, or GPUs on the CPUs directly and putting really high bandwidth connections between them.
sentences.zh: 都开始做一些有趣的事情，把 CPU 或 GPU 直接集成到 CPU 上，并在它们之间建立高带宽的连接。

sentences.en: So that's kind of interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以这挺有意思的。

sentences.en: But NVIDIA has a language that you use to do this general purpose programming for GPUs.
sentences.zh: 不过 NVIDIA 有一种专门用于对 GPU 进行通用编程的语言。

sentences.en: And AMD has their own as well.
sentences.zh: AMD 也有他们自己的语言。

sentences.en: But NVIDIA's is called CUDA.
sentences.zh: 但 NVIDIA 的语言叫做 CUDA。

sentences.en: And they, it's a kind of a dialect of C, which is limited.
sentences.zh: 而且它本质上是 C 语言的一个受限方言。

sentences.en: You can't do a lot of the same things you might be able to do in regular C or C++.
sentences.zh: 你在普通 C 或 C++ 中能做的事，有很多在里面是做不了的。

sentences.en: But for the most part, it's just a C program.
sentences.zh: 但大体上，它就是一个 C 程序。

sentences.en: And it runs, you know, maybe thousands or hundreds of thousands of threads.
sentences.zh: 它运行着，你知道，几千甚至几十万个线程。

sentences.en: And each one just does a little task.
sentences.zh: 每个线程只负责一个小任务。

sentences.en: So massively parallel.
sentences.zh: 这就是海量并行。

sentences.en: And that's really good for certain operations like image processing operations, graphics operations, certain kinds of, like, simulations, like Monte Carlo simulations, where you,
sentences.zh: 这非常适合某些特定的操作，比如图像处理操作、图形操作，以及某些类型的模拟，比如蒙特卡洛模拟，在这些模拟中，

sentences.en: you know, choose random numbers and, you know, run a little simulation based on that random number.
sentences.zh: 你选择随机数，然后基于该随机数运行一个小型的模拟。

sentences.en: Things like that can be really good.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情用这个效果会非常好。

sentences.en: But the problem is that the code between what you write for a CPU and what you write for a GPU are so very different from each other.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，你为 CPU 编写的代码和为 GPU 编写的代码有着天壤之别。

sentences.en: It can almost make the expense of going through creating a separate, you know, code base for your CUDA prograMs.
sentences.zh: 这几乎使得为你的 CUDA 程序专门去开发一套独立代码库的成本变得过高。

sentences.en: Unless you're one of these few cases that get, you know, a thousand X speed up from it, it almost makes that not worth it.
sentences.zh: 除非你是那少数能从中获得上千倍速度提升的幸运儿，否则这几乎不值得去做。

sentences.en: And it's better just to buy or pay more to get the latest and greatest CPU so that you can just have one code base.
sentences.zh: 更好的做法是花更多的钱购买最新最强大的 CPU，这样你只需要维护一个代码库就行了。

sentences.en: And yeah, and the other part of it, too, is, you know, the GPU, you have to communicate with it.
sentences.zh: 而且另一个问题是，你必须与 GPU 进行通信。

sentences.en: It's sort of like an external processor, you know, whereas the CPU, it's right on board.
sentences.zh: 它有点像一个外部处理器，而 CPU 则是板载集成在一起的。

sentences.en: And so because of that, debugging is much easier on the CPU.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，在 CPU 上的调试要容易得多。

sentences.en: Like, you could take a program that's running and just stop it and say, all right, right now, what's the state of the system?
sentences.zh: 比如，你可以让一个正在运行的程序停下来，然后说：“行，现在系统的状态是什么？”

sentences.en: Now, let's process one instruction.
sentences.zh: “现在，处理一条指令。”

sentences.en: Now, where are we at?
sentences.zh: “现在，我们运行到哪儿了？”

sentences.en: But, you know, because you have this GPU on a completely different card, you know, the debugging becomes much more difficult.
sentences.zh: 但是，因为这个 GPU 位于一张完全不同的显卡上，调试就会变得困难得多。

sentences.en: You can't do the kind of cool, hacky things that you can do, that debuggers do for a CPU.
sentences.zh: 你无法使用那些为 CPU 调试器所能做出的、那种炫酷且充满黑客技巧的操作。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Oh, and the other thing is that the pipe between the CPU and GPU, the PCI Express bus, is limited in its speed.
sentences.zh: 哦，还有一件事，那就是连接 CPU 和 GPU 的通道——PCI Express 总线，其速度是有限的。

sentences.en: You think it's really fast, but it's really not all that faSt.
sentences.zh: 你可能觉得它非常快，但实际上并没有那么快。

sentences.en: So there's all this overhead of sending data to the GPU to get processed and getting your results back.
sentences.zh: 所以这里面存在着各种开销，包括把数据发送到 GPU 进行处理，以及把结果取回来。

sentences.en: And so there's a, you know, crossover point where when your data gets big enough and parallel enough, it makes it's worth it to send it there and get it back.
sentences.zh: 因此存在一个临界点，当你的数据量足够大、并行度足够高时，把数据送过去再拿回来是划算的，

sentences.en: It's faster.
sentences.zh: 速度会更快。

sentences.en: But below that threshold is better to do it on the CPU.
sentences.zh: 但如果低于这个阈值，直接在 CPU 上处理反而更好。

sentences.en: But if your program has dynamic, you know, size of data, you kind of either have to have code in both and, you know, choose on your own which one to run.
sentences.zh: 但如果你的程序包含动态大小的数据，你要么得在两边都写代码，然后自己决定运行哪一个，

sentences.en: the screen size.

sentences.en: And then also for a certain set of encoding parameters because of the fact that, you know, they have hardware acceleration to do, for instance, H.264 decoding.

sentences.en: Time for the discussion of our programming language of the week, Lisp.
sentences.zh: 是时候讨论我们本周的编程语言了：Lisp。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Lisp is the language we're going to be talking about.
sentences.zh: Lisp就是我们要讨论的语言。

sentences.en: It's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 它真的很有趣。

sentences.en: It's definitely, if you're into computer science and sort of the understanding, like, the history and sort of the more, I guess, the less hands-on,
sentences.zh: 这绝对是，如果你对计算机科学感兴趣，并且想要理解历史，以及那种更偏向于——我想是不那么动手实践的，

sentences.en: the more kind of pie-in-the-sky theory and things like that.
sentences.zh: 更偏向于空中楼阁般的理论之类的内容的话。

sentences.en: This is a good language to know.
sentences.zh: 这门语言很值得了解。

sentences.en: It was actually invented before it was implemented.
sentences.zh: 它其实在被实现之前就被发明出来了。

sentences.en: So, someone, and do we have the person's name?
sentences.zh: 所以，有人——我们有这个人的名字吗？

sentences.en: Let me see.
sentences.zh: 我看看。

sentences.en: John McCarthy, back in 1958.
sentences.zh: 约翰·麦卡锡，早在1958年。

sentences.en: So, Lisp was a very old language.
sentences.zh: 所以，Lisp是一门非常古老的语言。

sentences.en: He kind of formalized this idea of Lisp and sort of the core functions that constitute the Lisp language and sort of proved that Lisp was Turing complete and things like that.
sentences.zh: 他将Lisp的这种理念以及构成Lisp语言的核心函数进行了形式化，并且证明了Lisp是图灵完备的诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: But before there was even an implementation.
sentences.zh: 但当时甚至还没有一个实现版本。

sentences.en: I mean, this was just all done in paper.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这一切都只是在纸上完成的。

sentences.en: It was a thought experiment, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一个思想实验，对吧？

sentences.en: And it wasn't until much later, actually, I guess a few years later, that Steve Russell created the first Lisp implementation.
sentences.zh: 直到很久以后，实际上我想是几年之后，史蒂夫·拉塞尔才创建了第一个Lisp实现。

sentences.en: So, yeah, so Lisp has a wide history.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，Lisp有着悠久的历史。

sentences.en: Because Lisp is so tied to computer science, there's just tons of different dialects of Lisp.
sentences.zh: 因为Lisp与计算机科学联系如此紧密，所以有大量不同的Lisp方言。

sentences.en: You know, there's Scheme and things like that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有Scheme之类的语言。

sentences.en: It seems to be probably the, how do you say this, like the most well-known, least-used programming language.
sentences.zh: 它似乎可以说是——怎么说呢——最广为人知、却又最少被使用的编程语言。

sentences.en: Like, people use it, but not every day.
sentences.zh: 就像是，人们会用它，但不是每天都用。

sentences.en: Like, people don't use it in their everyday jobs.
sentences.zh: 比如，人们在日常工作中不会使用它。

sentences.en: But it seems like everybody who goes through computer science learns it.
sentences.zh: 但似乎每个学过计算机科学的人都学过它。

sentences.en: Or even people who are just interested in computer programming will pick it up.
sentences.zh: 甚至是对计算机编程感兴趣的人也会去接触它。

sentences.en: And they'll at least play with it, if not learn to be experts in it.
sentences.zh: 他们至少会把玩一下，即使没有达到精通的水平。

sentences.en: You know, at least know it, but then not use it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，至少了解它，但随后并不使用它。

sentences.en: But, yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 不过，是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think, you know, part of the problems with Lisp, and we'll talk about this more in the weaknesses, but is that it's just, it's so fragmented, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，而且我认为，你知道，Lisp存在的问题之一——我们会在谈到缺点时更多地讨论这一点——就是它太碎片化了，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, this isn't really a problem with Lisp as much as just the, just, I guess, the social sort of, just the events that transpired.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这与其说是Lisp本身的问题，不如说是——我想是社会层面的那种，仅仅是历史事件的发展结果。

sentences.en: But Lisp is so fragmented.
sentences.zh: 但Lisp确实太碎片化了。

sentences.en: There's many different compilers for Lisp, or interpreters, I should say.
sentences.zh: Lisp有许多不同的编译器，或者我应该说解释器。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's so many different dialects.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，有太多不同的方言了。

sentences.en: And for a long time, none of the interpreters were open source.
sentences.zh: 在很长一段时间里，这些解释器都不是开源的。

sentences.en: So, you know, each one sort of had its own nuances.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，每一个都有它自己的细微差别。

sentences.en: And so this is, I feel like this is really kind of plagued Lisp.
sentences.zh: 因此我觉得这确实给Lisp带来了很多困扰。

sentences.en: But the two things that are sort of critical to Lisp are car and cooter.
sentences.zh: 但是对Lisp来说至关重要的两个东西是car和cdr。

sentences.en: So, C-A-R and C-D-R.
sentences.zh: 也就是C-A-R和C-D-R。

sentences.en: And the way this works is, think of everything in Lisp as being a pair.
sentences.zh: 它的工作原理是，把Lisp中的一切都看作是一个个的对（pair）。

sentences.en: And the pair is actually called cons, C-O-N-S.
sentences.zh: 而这个对实际上被称为cons，即C-O-N-S。

sentences.en: So, you have a pair of objects, but the objects themselves, they could be anything.
sentences.zh: 所以，你有一对对象，但对象本身可以是任何东西。

sentences.en: And to get, to go from a pair to the specific, like, elements in the pair, like the first and the second, you would call car to get at the first,
sentences.zh: 要想从一个对（pair）访问对中的具体元素，比如第一个和第二个，你会调用car来获取第一个，

sentences.en: or you'd call cooter to get at the second.
sentences.zh: 或者调用cdr来获取第二个。

sentences.en: And so just with cons, car, and cooter, that forms a basis for the entire Lisp language.
sentences.zh: 因此，仅仅通过cons、car和cdr，就构成了整个Lisp语言的基础。

sentences.en: A lot of it's based on lambda calculus, which gets into some pretty heavy stuff.
sentences.zh: 它很大一部分基于lambda演算，这就涉及一些相当深奥的内容了。

sentences.en: Basically, lambda calculus is sort of a formalism.
sentences.zh: 基本上，lambda演算是一种形式体系。

sentences.en: You know, we talked about first-order predicate calculus.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们之前讨论过一阶谓词演算。

sentences.en: We were talking about prologue.
sentences.zh: 我们在讨论Prolog时谈到过。

sentences.en: And so this is just another way of sort of representing numbers and the computations on those numbers.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是表示数字以及对这些数字进行计算的另一种方式。

sentences.en: And you can read about it more on Wikipedia.
sentences.zh: 你可以在维基百科上了解更多关于它的信息。

sentences.en: But understand that, similar to prologue, Lisp is sort of based on calculus.
sentences.zh: 但要明白，类似于Prolog，Lisp某种程度上也是基于演算的。

sentences.en: And so because of that, you can imagine it's not something you're going to write device drivers for, right?
sentences.zh: 正因如此，你可以想象它并不是那种你会用来编写设备驱动程序的语言，对吧？

sentences.en: So this is something that's kind of very theoretical.
sentences.zh: 所以这是非常偏向理论的东西。

sentences.en: However, there have been Lisp machines.
sentences.zh: 不过，曾经有过Lisp机。

sentences.en: Have you heard anything about this?
sentences.zh: 你听说过这个吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, it was a little bit before my time, I guess, although maybe I was still quite young when some of it was going on.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这大概比我的时代要早一点，我想，尽管当其中一些事情发生时，可能我还相当年轻。

sentences.en: But the Lisp machines was kind of an effort when the personal computers were first coming out to have a machine that was for individual users,
sentences.zh: 但Lisp机可以说是个人电脑刚问世时的一种尝试，旨在打造一台面向个人用户的机器，

sentences.en: which although didn't directly implement Lisp, so there weren't assembly-level commands that said, you know, the parts of the Lisp language directly.
sentences.zh: 尽管它并不直接实现Lisp，也就是说没有汇编级别的指令去直接对应Lisp语言的各个部分。

sentences.en: What it did was provide a really simple stack-based processor as opposed to a register-based processor,
sentences.zh: 它所做的是提供了一个非常简单的基于栈的处理器，而不是基于寄存器的处理器，

sentences.en: which I guess gets pretty in-depth and probably outside the scope for this discussion.
sentences.zh: 我想这涉及相当深入的底层知识，可能超出了本次讨论的范围。

sentences.en: But instead of register-based, it was stack-based.
sentences.zh: 但它不是基于寄存器的，而是基于栈的。

sentences.en: And the commands themselves were meant to be very easily derived by Lisp code.
sentences.zh: 而且指令本身被设计为可以非常容易地由Lisp代码推导出来。

sentences.en: So a Lisp code would translate into very few instructions, as opposed to on a normal register-based CPU, for instance, a single Lisp command may take many,
sentences.zh: 所以一段Lisp代码可以转化为极少的指令，相比之下，在普通的基于寄存器的CPU上，例如，一个简单的Lisp命令可能需要很多很多条机器指令来实现。

sentences.en: many machine instructions to implement.
sentences.zh: 机器指令来执行。

sentences.en: And so this processor architecture was put together in something called a Lisp machine that was meant to be easily programmed and efficient at writing and using and running Lisp prograMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种处理器架构被整合到了一种叫做Lisp机的设备中，旨在使其易于编程，并且在编写、使用和运行Lisp程序时非常高效。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, I mean, you know, think about the difference between, say, C and Lisp.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，你知道，想想C语言和Lisp之间的区别。

sentences.en: So in C, you know, just from a data perspective, in C you're dealing with arrays and pointers that point to different spots of memory.
sentences.zh: 所以在C语言中，仅从数据的角度来看，在C语言中你处理的是数组以及指向内存不同位置的指针。

sentences.en: And so you do pointer arithmetic.
sentences.zh: 所以你在做指针算术运算。

sentences.en: So, for example, if you have an array and you want to loop through the array, you would, you know, have a pointer at the beginning of the array and then you sort of increment.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，如果你有一个数组，并且你想遍历这个数组，你知道的，你会在数组的开头放一个指针，然后进行某种递增。

sentences.en: It's very numerical.
sentences.zh: 这非常依赖数值。

sentences.en: You just say, I want to push my pointer a little bit further and read the data over here and then push it further.
sentences.zh: 你只需要说，我想把我的指针再往前推一点，然后在这里读取数据，然后再往前推。

sentences.en: So, you're kind of like you'd read off a tape or a record or something like that.
sentences.zh: 所以，这有点像你从磁带、唱片或类似的东西上读取数据。

sentences.en: In Lisp, you don't have arrays.
sentences.zh: 在 Lisp 中，你没有数组。

sentences.en: What you have are, as I mentioned, these pairs.
sentences.zh: 正如我所提到的，你拥有的是这些序对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So you have pairs.
sentences.zh: 所以你拥有序对。

sentences.en: So if you want to have, say, a list, if you want to have an array, let's say, in Lisp, then what you would have is you'd have a pair.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你想拥有，比方说，一个列表，如果你想在 Lisp 中拥有一个数组，比方说，那么你会拥有的就是一个序对。

sentences.en: The left, the first element in the pair would have some item in your liSt.
sentences.zh: 左边，序对中的第一个元素将包含你列表中的某个项目。

sentences.en: Let's say it's a list of numbers.
sentences.zh: 假设这是一个数字列表。

sentences.en: So the first element in your pair would have the number, say, four.
sentences.zh: 所以你序对中的第一个元素将包含这个数字，比如说，四。

sentences.en: And the second element of your pair would have a pair in it.
sentences.zh: 而你序对的第二个元素将包含一个序对。

sentences.en: And in that pair, the first element would have a number, let's say, two.
sentences.zh: 在这个序对中，第一个元素将包含一个数字，比方说，二。

sentences.en: And the second element would have another pair.
sentences.zh: 而第二个元素将包含另一个序对。

sentences.en: So you see, everything is done in pairs.
sentences.zh: 所以你看，一切都是用序对完成的。

sentences.en: And any of the two elements in the pair can be either an atom, which is, you know, a number or a word or, you know, something that's immutable, something that can't change.
sentences.zh: 序对中的任意两个元素既可以是一个原子，你知道的，它是一个数字、一个单词，或者，你知道的，某种不可变的东西，某种不能改变的东西。

sentences.en: Like a constant, right?
sentences.zh: 就像一个常量，对吧？

sentences.en: Or it's either a constant or it's another pair.
sentences.zh: 要么它是一个常量，要么它又是另一个序对。

sentences.en: Or it's nil.
sentences.zh: 或者它是 nil。

sentences.en: Those are your three.
sentences.zh: 这就是你的三种类型。

sentences.en: Those are the only three, you know, things that can exiSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这些是仅有的三种可以存在的东西。

sentences.en: So as we mentioned in JavaScript, where there was only four things, in JavaScript, there's nil, you know, array, object, and literal.
sentences.zh: 所以正如我们在 JavaScript 中提到的，那里只有四种东西，在 JavaScript 中，有 nil，你知道的，数组、对象和字面量。

sentences.en: In Lisp, there's only atom, which is the same as literal, pair, and nil.
sentences.zh: 而在 Lisp 中，只有原子（这和字面量相同）、序对和 nil。

sentences.en: There's only three.
sentences.zh: 总共只有三种。

sentences.en: So, you know, you would think that because it's so simple that, oh, you know, you must be, like, really low level.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，你可能会认为，因为它如此简单，哦，你知道的，它一定非常底层。

sentences.en: Like, you must use this for drivers because it's such a simple language.
sentences.zh: 就像，你一定得用它来写驱动程序，因为这是一门如此简单的语言。

sentences.en: But actually making the language very simple is really what gives it the power and gives it the ability to represent incredibly complex things.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，让语言变得非常简单，才正是赋予它强大能力和代表极其复杂事物能力的原因。

sentences.en: And we'll talk about this a little more when we get to the strengths.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈到它的优势时，我们会更多地讨论这一点。

sentences.en: But understand that, you know, a machine, a regular machine that just has a bank of memory where you can just do malloc and get arrays,
sentences.zh: 但要明白，你知道的，一台普通的机器，它只拥有一块内存，你可以在上面直接调用 malloc 并获取数组，

sentences.en: that kind of machine doesn't run Lisp very efficiently, especially, you know, 30 years ago, 40 years ago.
sentences.zh: 这种机器运行 Lisp 的效率并不高，特别是在，你知道的，30 年前，40 年前。

sentences.en: So the idea of the Lisp machine was, let's make a machine with the constraints of Lisp in mind.
sentences.zh: 所以 Lisp 机器的想法是，让我们设计一台考虑到 Lisp 局限性的机器。

sentences.en: Let's make a machine that deals with things in terms of pairs.
sentences.zh: 让我们设计一台用序对来处理事务的机器。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I mean, it seems like they were fairly successful at doing that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们在这方面似乎相当成功。

sentences.en: It was just that the competition in the market was somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 只是市场上的竞争在别处。

sentences.en: It was in the traditional register-based machines running C.
sentences.zh: 它在运行 C 语言的传统寄存器机上。

sentences.en: And so it seems like there have been many of these instances in the even short-lived software world where even if something made sense or was technically superior, it won out.
sentences.zh: 因此看起来，在甚至可以说是短命的软件世界里，有很多这样的例子：即使某种东西合乎情理或在技术上更优秀，它也没有胜出。

sentences.en: Something else won out because of just market inertia or, you know, happenstance or various other things.
sentences.zh: 由于市场惯性、你知道的，偶然性或各种其他原因，其他东西胜出了。

sentences.en: And, you know, the Lisp machine kind of fits in that category.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，Lisp 机器有点符合那个范畴。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'd like to think that, you know, being an AI person and being sympathetic to Lisp, I like to think that it's sort of the grandfather of many other languages.
sentences.zh: 是的，我愿意认为，你知道的，作为一个人工智能从业者并且对 Lisp 抱有同理心，我愿意认为它是许多其他语言的祖父。

sentences.en: Like, you know, other languages like Python, JavaScript, which, you know, is based on – JavaScript was based on Scheme, right?
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道的，其他语言如 Python、JavaScript，你知道的，它是基于——JavaScript 是基于 Scheme 的，对吧？

sentences.en: It was inspired by Scheme.
sentences.zh: 它受 Scheme 启发。

sentences.en: It was influenced, yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 它受到了影响，对，对，对。

sentences.en: Yeah, and Scheme is a dialect of Lisp, so there you go.
sentences.zh: 是的，Scheme 是 Lisp 的一种方言，所以就是这样。

sentences.en: And, you know, even MATLAB, which is now very popular, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，甚至现在非常流行的 MATLAB，你知道的，

sentences.en: Lisp is sort of the grandfather of all interpreted languages and is a good source of sort of inspiration for languages that came after and offered, you know,
sentences.zh: Lisp 可以说是所有解释型语言的祖父，并且是后来那些语言的良好灵感来源，这些语言提供了，你知道的，

sentences.en: much more boosts in productivity, you know, without all of the hindrances that Lisp has.
sentences.zh: 生产力的大幅提升，你知道的，却没有 Lisp 拥有的所有那些阻碍。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, so as we mentioned, there's many dialects,
sentences.zh: 对，对，所以正如我们所提到的，有很多方言，

sentences.en: but one of the reasons why there's so many dialects is because it's really easy to write an interpreter or a compiler for Lisp.
sentences.zh: 但之所以有这么多方言，原因之一是因为为 Lisp 编写解释器或编译器真的非常容易。

sentences.en: In fact, you know, as we mentioned with the, you know, become a good programmer and six really hard steps, the author even mentions that, hey,
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道的，正如我们之前提到的那个，“成为优秀程序员的六个艰难步骤”，作者甚至提到，嘿，

sentences.en: you should write a Lisp interpreter as one of the – as your language, you know, because it's a good start.
sentences.zh: 你应该把编写一个 Lisp 解释器作为你的语言项目之一——因为这是一个好的开始。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's so few things you actually – well, I mean, it seems tricky.
sentences.zh: 是的，你实际需要的东西真的很少——嗯，我是说，这看起来很棘手。

sentences.en: At the start, it seems so easy to get started because there's so few things you have to implement.
sentences.zh: 一开始，上手似乎很容易，因为你需要实现的东西实在太少了。

sentences.en: Yeah, and keep in mind that – and this is true for all languages.
sentences.zh: 是的，请记住——所有语言都是如此。

sentences.en: I don't know if we've mentioned this before, but most languages are written in themselves.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我们以前是否提到过这一点，但大多数语言都是用它们自己编写的。

sentences.en: So we have talked about this where, you know, we talked about Python being batteries included,
sentences.zh: 所以我们讨论过这一点，你知道的，我们讨论过 Python 是“内置电池”的，

sentences.en: where there's a huge corpus of tools that you have that are available to you when you start programming.
sentences.zh: 当你开始编程时，有一大堆工具库可供你使用。

sentences.en: The vast majority of those tools are written in Python.
sentences.zh: 其中绝大多数工具都是用 Python 编写的。

sentences.en: This is true even of, you know, C and Lisp and other languages, just to a lesser extent.
sentences.zh: 即使对于，你知道的，C、Lisp 和其他语言也是如此，只不过程度稍轻一些。

sentences.en: So, you know, 99% of Lisp is written in Lisp.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，99% 的 Lisp 都是用 Lisp 编写的。

sentences.en: And, you know, if you could take, like, the common Lisp libraries and, you know, use your own interpreter, you could really have your own Lisp, like,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，如果你能拿走，比如，Common Lisp 的库，并且，你知道的，使用你自己的解释器，你真的可以在一天内拥有你自己的、类似于 Lisp 的、

sentences.en: fully featured interpreter in a day.
sentences.zh: 功能齐全的解释器。

sentences.en: I mean, of course, it wouldn't be faSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当然，它不会很快。

sentences.en: It would be nothing like C-Lisp.
sentences.zh: 它和 C-Lisp 毫无可比性。

sentences.en: But, you know, it still would be fun.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，它仍然会很有趣。

sentences.en: You know, it's a toy to play with.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这只是个好玩的玩具。

sentences.en: And it seems like the other thing is that there are a lot of people who take Lisp and use it as kind of an intermediate language where you write something in Lisp and then you compile.
sentences.zh: 而且看起来另一件事是，有很多人把 Lisp 当作一种中间语言来使用，你用 Lisp 编写一些东西，然后进行编译。

sentences.en: Like, we talked about people doing this to JavaScript before, but people kind of use Lisp as an input language to the compiler, I guess,
sentences.zh: 就像我们之前讨论过人们对 JavaScript 做的那样，但人们有点把 Lisp 用作编译器的输入语言，我猜，

sentences.en: and then compile it to some other form of a language.
sentences.zh: 然后把它编译成某种其他形式的语言。

sentences.en: So, there's Clojure, which is C-L-O-J-U-R-E, as opposed to, we talked a little bit about the Clojure kit tools last week or last episode.
sentences.zh: 所以，有 Clojure，即 C-L-O-J-U-R-E，与我们上周或上一集简要讨论过的 Clojure kit 工具相对。

sentences.en: And that is implementing Lisp on top of Java.
sentences.zh: 那是基于 Java 之上实现 Lisp。

sentences.en: So, using the Java virtual machine and using Lisp as kind of, I guess, what is that, the front end to it and saying, how do we do that?
sentences.zh: 所以，使用 Java 虚拟机，并把 Lisp 用作某种，我猜，那是什么，它的前端，然后说，我们该怎么做？

sentences.en: And it's got a lot of popularity.
sentences.zh: 而且它赢得了很高的人气。

sentences.en: And there's also the, everybody kind of has their own little ways about some of the finer nuances of the language.
sentences.zh: 而且还有，每个人对这门语言的一些更精细的细微差别都有自己的一小套看法。

sentences.en: And so, each of those tends to kind of get its own spin-out dialect, which initially starts out really close to the one it started from, but then slowly drifts away over time.
sentences.zh: 因此，其中每一个往往都会衍生出自己的分支出方言，它们最初非常接近其发源的语言，但随后随着时间的推移慢慢偏离。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, so, some of the strengths of Lisp.
sentences.zh: 是的，那么，Lisp 的一些优势。

sentences.en: Lisp, one of the strengths is that it has very, very efficient hash tables.
sentences.zh: Lisp 的优势之一是它拥有非常、非常高效的哈希表。

sentences.en: And this is tied directly to the fact that there's so few data types.
sentences.zh: 这直接与数据类型极少这一事实挂钩。

sentences.en: You know, it does a lot of sort of, like, clever tricks with the pairs, and it can actually store a ton of data in a hash table very efficiently by sort of reusing the same data.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它对序对做了很多类似于巧妙把戏的操作，通过某种复用相同的数据，它实际上可以在哈希表中非常高效地存储大量数据。

sentences.en: Lisp is amazing at this.
sentences.zh: Lisp 在这方面太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, we should explain what a hash table is.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们应该解释一下什么是哈希表。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, you've probably never done that.
sentences.zh: 哦，对，你可能从来没做过这个。

sentences.en: So, yeah, so a hash table is something that essentially maps one data type to another.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，所以哈希表本质上是将一种数据类型映射到另一种数据类型的工具。

sentences.en: So, or one value.
sentences.zh: 所以，或者映射到一个值。

sentences.en: Yeah, I guess one, yeah, one value.
sentences.zh: 是的，我猜是一个，是的，一个值。

sentences.en: Maybe that's a better way of saying it.
sentences.zh: 也许这是更好的说法。

sentences.en: Essentially maps one value to another.
sentences.zh: 本质上是将一个值映射到另一个值。

sentences.en: So, for example, let's say you wanted to store the days of the week.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，假设你想存储星期几。

sentences.en: So, if you put in, you know, zero, you got Monday.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你输入，你知道的，零，你得到星期一。

sentences.en: If you put in one, you got Tuesday, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你输入一，你得到星期二，对吧？

sentences.en: So, in C, you could just have an array.
sentences.zh: 所以，在 C 语言中，你只需拥有一个数组。

sentences.en: And at the array index zero, you would just hold the string, a pointer to the string Monday.
sentences.zh: 在数组索引零处，你只需保存一个字符串，即指向字符串“星期一”的指针。

sentences.en: And one, you'd hold Tuesday, so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 而在索引一处，你保存“星期二”，以此类推。

sentences.en: And then you'd say, you know, days, open bracket, you know, two to get Wednesday, right?
sentences.zh: 然后你会说，你知道的，days，左括号，你知道的，二，来获取星期三，对吧？

sentences.en: What if you wanted to go backwards?
sentences.zh: 如果你想倒过来呢？

sentences.en: Like, what if someone gave you the string and you wanted to return what day of the week it was in numbers?
sentences.zh: 比如，如果有人给你这个字符串，而你想返回它是星期几的数字呢？

sentences.en: So, if someone gave you Monday, you wanted to return zero.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果有人给你“星期一”，你想返回零。

sentences.en: So, in this case, you'd have to use essentially a map.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这种情况下，你基本上必须使用一个映射（map）。

sentences.en: And the map would have to map strings to numbers.
sentences.zh: 而这个映射必须将字符串映射到数字。

sentences.en: See, an array, you can think of an array as a map, which maps numbers to something else, whatever's in the array.
sentences.zh: 看，一个数组，你可以把数组想象成一个映射，它将数字映射到其他东西，无论数组里有什么。

sentences.en: But whenever you need to map something that isn't a number, let's say you need to map, you know, a floating point number or, as I mentioned, a string.
sentences.zh: 但每当你需要映射不是数字的东西时，比方说你需要映射，你知道的，浮点数，或者正如我所提到的，字符串。

sentences.en: Or maybe you need to map a chessboard, like the entire board, like a whole class with the pieces and where they are.
sentences.zh: 或者也许你需要映射一个国际象棋棋盘，比如整个棋盘，就像一个包含棋子及其位置的完整类。

sentences.en: You need to map that to a number.
sentences.zh: 你需要将它映射到一个数字。

sentences.en: To do something like that, you have to use a map.
sentences.zh: 要做到这一点，你必须使用映射。

sentences.en: And one very common map implementation of a map is a hash table.
sentences.zh: 而映射的一种非常常见的实现方式就是哈希表。

sentences.en: What a hash table does is it takes, it basically is based on the principle that you don't actually need the key.
sentences.zh: 哈希表的作用是，它基本上基于这样一个原则：你实际上不需要这个键。

sentences.en: So, in other words, I don't actually need to store the string Monday in this table.
sentences.zh: 所以，换句话说，我实际上不需要在这个表中存储字符串“星期一”。

sentences.en: You know, what I need is when I get the string Monday, I need to know to return zero.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我需要的是当我拿到字符串“星期一”时，我知道该返回零。

sentences.en: But that doesn't necessarily mean that I need to hold Monday in the table.
sentences.zh: 但这并不一定意味着我必须把“星期一”保存在表中。

sentences.en: So, that sounds a little confusing, but take, for example, let's say that your hash table, instead of storing the whole string, it just stored the first two letters.
sentences.zh: 所以，这听起来有点令人困惑，但举个例子，假设你的哈希表不存储整个字符串，它只存储前两个字母。

sentences.en: So, that would be sufficient, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，这就足够了，对吧？

sentences.en: If someone passed in Monday, then I would just take the first two letters, M-O, and just look for that in the table.
sentences.zh: 如果有人传入“星期一”，那么我只需取前两个字母，M-O，然后在表中查找它。

sentences.en: And that would return zero.
sentences.zh: 那就会返回零。

sentences.en: And I've saved some data.
sentences.zh: 而我节省了一些数据。

sentences.en: I didn't have to store all of Monday.
sentences.zh: 我不必存储全部的“星期一”。

sentences.en: Now, you know, I couldn't use one letter, because if I did, then Tuesday and Thursday would both map to the same location.
sentences.zh: 现在，你知道的，我不能只用一个字母，因为如果我这样做了，那么“星期二”（Tuesday）和“星期四”（Thursday）都会映射到同一个位置。

sentences.en: That's called a collision, right?
sentences.zh: 这叫做冲突（collision），对吧？

sentences.en: And so, there's ways to deal with that even, so it's not the end of the world.
sentences.zh: 所以，甚至有办法处理这种情况，所以这不是世界末日。

sentences.en: But, you know, I could store two letters and save a lot of data.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，我可以存储两个字母并节省大量数据。

sentences.en: And so, hash tables, you know, there's a lot to it.
sentences.zh: 所以，哈希表，你知道的，这里面学问很多。

sentences.en: You know, if you're really good at hash tables, hash tables are sort of the backbone of just about everything in computer science,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你非常擅长哈希表，哈希表可以说是计算机科学中几乎所有东西的支柱，

sentences.en: especially distributed processing or, you know, web and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 特别是分布式处理或者，你知道的，网络等等。

sentences.en: So, it would take a whole show, but in a nutshell, you know, Lisp and the way Lisp works, the objects in Lisp are very hash friendly.
sentences.zh: 所以，这需要整整一期节目，但简而言之，你知道的，Lisp 以及 Lisp 的工作方式，Lisp 中的对象对哈希非常友好。

sentences.en: And on top of that, Lisp can do a lot of object reuse.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，Lisp 可以进行大量对象的复用。

sentences.en: So, it can implement hash tables very efficiently, very quickly.
sentences.zh: 因此，它可以非常高效、非常快地实现哈希表。

sentences.en: It can implement them without using a lot of memory.
sentences.zh: 它可以在不占用大量内存的情况下实现它们。

sentences.en: And this is really important for the applications, which we'll talk about later.
sentences.zh: 这对于我们稍后要讨论的应用来说非常重要。

sentences.en: So, do you have any other strengths for Lisp?
sentences.zh: 那么，你对 Lisp 还有其他优势要说吗？

sentences.en: So, one thing that, well, I guess this is one of those, it could be a strength and could be a weakness, is that you can use Lisp to parse itself.
sentences.zh: 所以有一点，嗯，我想这是那种既可以是优势也可以是劣势的特性，就是你可以用 Lisp 来解析它自己。

sentences.en: So, the difference between data and instructions in a C++, Java, Python program is very clear.
sentences.zh: 因此，在 C++、Java、Python 程序中，数据和指令之间的区别非常清晰。

sentences.en: It's very much, here's my code and here's the data I'm storing.
sentences.zh: 这非常明确，这是我的代码，这是我存储的数据。

sentences.en: I'm assigning this data to this variable.
sentences.zh: 我正在将这些数据赋值给这个变量。

sentences.en: And only in a few kind of edge cases where you might talk about function pointers or, you know,
sentences.zh: 只有在少数几种边缘情况下，你可能会谈论函数指针，或者，你知道的，

sentences.en: some kind of obscure things where your variable stores a pointer to code or code somewhere.
sentences.zh: 某些晦涩的事情，你的变量存储指向代码的指针或某处的代码。

sentences.en: But that isn't the usual case.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是通常的情况。

sentences.en: It doesn't normally happen.
sentences.zh: 这通常不会发生。

sentences.en: But in Lisp, you can have your program is represented as these pairs.
sentences.zh: 但在 Lisp 中，你可以让你的程序由这些序对表示。

sentences.en: So, you can, this is very easy to intermix both the data and the program.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以，这非常容易将数据和程序混合在一起。

sentences.en: And that means that you can manipulate the program.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你可以操纵程序。

sentences.en: So, that's known as self-modification.
sentences.zh: 所以这被称为自修改。

sentences.en: So, when the code, as it's running, changes the code that's running.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，代码在运行的同时，会改变正在运行的代码。

sentences.en: And in Lisp, this is easy to do because the, like I said, there's no real distinction between data and the program.
sentences.zh: 在 Lisp 中，这很容易做到，因为正如我所说，数据和程序之间没有真正的区别。

sentences.en: And that's a strength.
sentences.zh: 这是一个优势。

sentences.en: That gives you, there's some really powerful techniques that you can do and that make really efficient code.
sentences.zh: 它赋予了你一些非常强大的技术，你可以用它们编写出非常高效的代码。

sentences.en: It also happens to be something that can be very hard to understand.
sentences.zh: 它同时也恰好是那种非常难以理解的东西。

sentences.en: But it's one of those, with great power comes great responsibility.
sentences.zh: 但这就是那句名言，能力越大，责任越大。

sentences.en: If you use it wisely, it can be very powerful.
sentences.zh: 如果你明智地使用它，它会非常强大。

sentences.en: And if you use it poorly, it can cause probleMs.
sentences.zh: 如果你用得不好，它就会引发问题。

sentences.en: But Lisp is really good at doing that.
sentences.zh: 但 Lisp 在这方面真的很擅长。

sentences.en: Look at, like, the roguelike, for example.
sentences.zh: 比如说，看看类 Rogue 游戏。

sentences.en: So, let's say you're making a simple roguelike game following the 15 steps.
sentences.zh: 所以，假设你正按照这 15 个步骤制作一个简单的类 Rogue 游戏。

sentences.en: And, you know, you make a sword.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，你造了一把剑。

sentences.en: And, you know, you have this sword class.
sentences.zh: 而且，你懂的，你有了这个剑的类。

sentences.en: And you have some data.
sentences.zh: 并且你有一些数据。

sentences.en: Like, you have the great sword, where the name is great.
sentences.zh: 比如，你有一把大剑，名字就叫“大”。

sentences.en: And it does, like, 10 damage.
sentences.zh: 它能造成，比如说，10 点伤害。

sentences.en: And then you have, like, the awesome sword.
sentences.zh: 然后你还有，比如，酷炫剑。

sentences.en: So, you have some text file.
sentences.zh: 所以，你有一个文本文件。

sentences.en: And the text file just has, you know, great sword, comma, 10.
sentences.zh: 这个文本文件里面写着，大剑，逗号，10。

sentences.en: Awesome sword, comma, 20.
sentences.zh: 酷炫剑，逗号，20。

sentences.en: You know, light sword, comma, 30.
sentences.zh: 还有，轻剑，逗号，30。

sentences.en: And so, like, then you write some C program that looks at your text file.
sentences.zh: 于是，接着你写了一些 C 语言程序来读取你的文本文件。

sentences.en: And then it says, okay, create, you know, create a great sword.
sentences.zh: 然后它说，好的，创建，你知道的，创建一把大剑。

sentences.en: Create an awesome sword.
sentences.zh: 创建一把酷炫剑。

sentences.en: And then put these somewhere in memory so that I can fill my world full of great and awesome swords.
sentences.zh: 然后把这些东西放到内存的某个地方，这样我就可以让我的世界充满各种大剑和酷炫剑。

sentences.en: But what if I wanted a flaming sword?
sentences.zh: 但如果我想要一把烈焰剑呢？

sentences.en: And when you hit somebody with it, they caught on fire.
sentences.zh: 当你用它击中某人时，他们会着火。

sentences.en: And there was all this code and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 还有所有这些代码之类的东西。

sentences.en: Well, you know, that can't really go in the text file.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，那可没法真正放进文本文件里。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: You can't describe the flames.
sentences.zh: 你没法描述那些火焰。

sentences.en: Yeah, you can't describe the flames and the effect and the person catching on fire and what that means.
sentences.zh: 对，你没法描述火焰、效果、人着火的状况以及这意味着什么。

sentences.en: All that logic.
sentences.zh: 所有这些逻辑。

sentences.en: You can't just put that in the text file.
sentences.zh: 你不能只是把它塞进文本文件里。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, you'd have to put it in the C file and then know that, oh, a flaming sword has this, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你得把它写进 C 语言文件里，然后还得知道，哦，烈焰剑有这个特性，对吧？

sentences.en: But with Lisp, you can just, your data and your code is the same thing.
sentences.zh: 但在 Lisp 中，你可以直接让你的数据和代码是同一个东西。

sentences.en: So, you would have, in Lisp, you would have, you know, a pair.
sentences.zh: 所以，在 Lisp 中你会有一个，你知道的，序对（pair）。

sentences.en: And the pair, the first element would be the name.
sentences.zh: 这个序对的第一个元素是名字。

sentences.en: And the second element would be a pair, which would have the, you know, damage.
sentences.zh: 第二个元素是另一个序对，里面包含着，你知道的，伤害值。

sentences.en: And then, you know, the third element there could be an entire Lisp program, which is what happens when you hit someone with the sword.
sentences.zh: 然后，第三个元素可以是一个完整的 Lisp 程序，也就是当你用这把剑击中别人时会发生的事情。

sentences.en: And you don't have to worry about reading your data from the text file like you do in C and, like, you know, creating sword objects based on the data in the text file.
sentences.zh: 你不用像在 C 语言中那样担心从文本文件里读取数据，也不用像那样根据文本文件里的数据去创建剑对象。

sentences.en: You just load that Lisp file and it's done.
sentences.zh: 你只需加载那个 Lisp 文件，就大功告成了。

sentences.en: So, yeah, you could do some awesome stuff with it.
sentences.zh: 所以，没错，你可以用它做出一些超棒的东西。

sentences.en: But, yeah, I mean, it makes it very difficult to debug and things like that.
sentences.zh: 不过，话又说回来，这会让调试变得非常困难，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So, yeah, it's kind of a wild thing that you have at your fingertips.
sentences.zh: 所以，这确实是你触手可及的一种挺疯狂的东西。

sentences.en: So, with all of the, these things are nice features, everything's a pair, and the language provides some abstraction.
sentences.zh: 因此，有了所有这些不错的特性——万物皆为序对，且语言提供了一定的抽象机制——

sentences.en: So, I guess we should say that even though everything under the hood is a pair, the languages allow you to not have to literally, if you want to make a list,
sentences.zh: 我想我们应该说明，尽管底层一切都是序对，但这些语言允许你不必字面上地去……如果你想创建一个列表，

sentences.en: have, you know, a pair where the second element is another pair and the second element is another pair,
sentences.zh: 非要弄出一个“第二个元素是另一个序对，而那个序对的第二个元素又是另一个序对”的结构，

sentences.en: they give you the power to just, you know, make one long list and do that pairing for you.
sentences.zh: 它们赋予了你强大的能力，让你只需创建一个长长的列表，就能替你完成这种配对。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a good point.
sentences.zh: 对，说得好。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I was just thinking about that because one of the weaknesses, though, that even with that,
sentences.zh: 所以，我刚才就在想这个，因为它的一个弱点，即使有了这些特性，

sentences.en: Lisp tends to have a ton of parentheses, and parentheses are what are used to kind of wrap each pair.
sentences.zh: Lisp 往往有大量的括号，而括号正是用来包裹每个序对的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it's, you know, they've done a lot to make it less painful.
sentences.zh: 对，我是说，他们已经做了很多努力来减轻这种痛苦。

sentences.en: So, as Patrick mentioned, if you have 10 items, you can just put a single parentheses around them,
sentences.zh: 所以，正如帕特里克提到的，如果你有 10 个项目，你只需在它们周围加一对括号，

sentences.en: and Lisp under the hood knows that it's like a bunch of pairs that are all chained together.
sentences.zh: Lisp 在底层就会知道这就像是一堆串联在一起的序对。

sentences.en: But the fact is, yeah, I mean, there's just, you're dealing with pairs.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，你就是在跟序对打交道。

sentences.en: And as you might imagine, there's a lot of data, a lot of variables you might have in your code.
sentences.zh: 正如你所想象的，代码里会有大量的数据和变量。

sentences.en: But you're going to have a ton of parentheses.
sentences.zh: 但你会遇到成吨的括号。

sentences.en: That's kind of endemic of Lisp prograMs.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是 Lisp 编程的顽疾。

sentences.en: So, fortunately, if you use Emacs, you can, it'll match up the, or actually, I guess, most modern, or not even modern.
sentences.zh: 好在如果你使用 Emacs，你可以让它帮你匹配，或者实际上，我想大多数现代编辑器——甚至算不上现代，

sentences.en: Most editors will do this for you, but it'll help you match up the parentheses.
sentences.zh: 大多数编辑器都会为你做这件事，它们会帮你在括号间进行匹配。

sentences.en: But, yeah, it still can make things a little cumbersome.
sentences.zh: 不过，它还是会让事情变得有点繁琐。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's not really a weakness, but it is something when people look at Lisp code, some languages you don't exactly know at first, like C++ and Java.
sentences.zh: 这倒算不上是一个致命弱点，但当人们看 Lisp 代码时——有些语言你一开始可能看不懂，比如 C++ 和 Java。

sentences.en: Sometimes you have to kind of look at certain lines of code to kind of understand what it is.
sentences.zh: 有时你得仔细端详某些代码行才能明白它的意思。

sentences.en: When you look at Lisp code, it's really easy to tell because you just look for all the parentheses.
sentences.zh: 而你看 Lisp 代码时，一眼就能看出来，因为你只需要寻找所有的括号。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, think about this.
sentences.zh: 对，想想看。

sentences.en: As we mentioned, again, everything's a pair.
sentences.zh: 正如我们再次提到的，万物皆为序对。

sentences.en: So, if you want to add two numbers, what you really want, you want a pair of a plus sign and a pair of a 2 and a 3 underneath it.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想把两个数字相加，你真正想要的是：一个加号构成的序对，以及它下方由数字 2 和 3 构成的序对。

sentences.en: So, you have, now, with CLisp and more advanced Lisp, you can take away the parentheses around the 2 and a 3.
sentences.zh: 在 Common Lisp 和更高级的 Lisp 中，你可以去掉数字 2 和 3 外面的括号。

sentences.en: But, you're going to have a parentheses and then the plus sign and then 2 and 3.
sentences.zh: 但是，你依然会有一个括号，然后是加号，接着是 2 和 3。

sentences.en: That's another thing about Lisp is that everything is in prefix notation.
sentences.zh: Lisp 的另一个特点是所有东西都采用前缀表示法。

sentences.en: So, if you want to do 2 plus 3, you actually want to do plus 2, 3.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想做 2 加 3，你实际要写的是：加号、2、3。

sentences.en: And so, because it's in prefix, let's say you wanted to do 2 plus 3 minus 4.
sentences.zh: 正因为它是前缀的，假设你想做 2 加 3 减 4。

sentences.en: It would actually be plus minus 2, 3, 4.
sentences.zh: 它实际上会变成：加号、减号、2、3、4。

sentences.en: So, now, that doesn't make any sense, right?
sentences.zh: 这完全说不通，对吧？

sentences.en: Because the order of operations, you don't really know.
sentences.zh: 因为运算符的顺序，你根本无从得知。

sentences.en: You know, prefix notation doesn't really give you order of operations.
sentences.zh: 前缀表示法并不能真正体现运算顺序。

sentences.en: So, to deal with all that, you specify the order explicitly.
sentences.zh: 所以为了处理这一切，你得显式地指定顺序。

sentences.en: So, to do 2 plus 3 minus 4, you'd actually do open parentheses, open parentheses, minus sign, or, yeah, minus sign, open parentheses, plus sign, 2, 3, close parentheses, four,
sentences.zh: 因此，要计算 2 加 3 减 4，你实际上得这样写：左括号，左括号，减号，或者说，减号，左括号，加号，2，3，右括号，4，

sentences.en: close parentheses.
sentences.zh: 右括号。

sentences.en: So, just to do something that simple, you already needed four parentheses, like two opening and two closing.
sentences.zh: 所以，仅仅为了做这么简单的事情，你已经需要四个括号了，也就是两个左括号和两个右括号。

sentences.en: So, it can get pretty cumbersome.
sentences.zh: 所以它可能会变得相当繁琐。

sentences.en: But one of the other, you know, weaknesses of Lisp, beyond just the syntax, is that it doesn't have direct memory access.
sentences.zh: 但 Lisp 的另一个弱点，除了语法本身之外，就是它没有直接的内存访问能力。

sentences.en: And it doesn't really have much in the way of hardware access.
sentences.zh: 而且它在硬件访问方面也做得很有限。

sentences.en: So, people have written extensions.
sentences.zh: 因此人们编写了各种扩展。

sentences.en: But, you know, for the most part, it's not really designed to, you know, fit the model of a computer.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，它并不是为了契合计算机的模型而设计的。

sentences.en: And this is one of the, you know, things that really hurt Lisp.
sentences.zh: 这也是真正伤害 Lisp 的原因之一。

sentences.en: But that's, you know, that's what inspired people to make the Lisp machines that they did, you know, 20, 30 years ago.
sentences.zh: 但这正是激发人们在 20、30 年前制造出那些 Lisp 机的原因所在。

sentences.en: Yeah, and that's really fundamental, being able to manipulate specific memory locations.
sentences.zh: 是的，这非常根本，也就是能够操作特定的内存地址。

sentences.en: Because that's, you know, for people who have never done it before, it may not be obvious.
sentences.zh: 因为对于从未接触过的人来说，这可能并不显而易见。

sentences.en: But that's how, at the lowest level, all the drivers work.
sentences.zh: 但在底层，所有的驱动程序都是这样工作的。

sentences.en: So, the things that control hardware all come down to basically putting certain values at certain memory locations.
sentences.zh: 控制硬件的东西，归根结底就是在特定的内存地址写入特定的值。

sentences.en: And doing that causes something to happen electrically on that peripheral device.
sentences.zh: 这样做会使那个外设在电气上产生某些反应。

sentences.en: And that's how device drivers are written.
sentences.zh: 设备驱动程序就是这样编写的。

sentences.en: And so, if you don't have the ability to control exactly what the contents of a certain memory location are, then you're not going to be able to control that device.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你没有能力精确控制某个内存地址的内容，你就无法控制那个设备。

sentences.en: And you can't write device drivers.
sentences.zh: 你也无法编写设备驱动程序。

sentences.en: And that's what a lot of low-level code is working with, those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 许多底层代码处理的就是这类事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, you know, a lot of people are probably too young.
sentences.zh: 是啊，可能很多人都太年轻了。

sentences.en: A lot of people listening to the show are too young to have serial mouse.
sentences.zh: 听节目的很多人都太年轻了，没赶上过串行鼠标。

sentences.en: But when I started learning about computers, I had a serial mouse.

sentences.en: like Python, but LISP was really sort of only, you know, useful to academics at the time when it was most popular.

sentences.en: So, you already kind of mentioned that LISP is used a lot in the artificial intelligence community.
sentences.zh: 你们用它来做什么类型的事情？

sentences.en: What kinds of things do you guys use it for?
sentences.zh: 对，Lisp 曾在规划（planning）中被大量使用。

sentences.en: Yeah, so LISP was very, was used a lot in planning.
sentences.zh: 那么，我来稍微解释一下什么是规划。

sentences.en: And so, let me explain a little bit of what planning is.
sentences.zh: 规划基本上就是在特定的空间中进行搜索，并找出采取哪些行动才是最优解。

sentences.en: Planning is basically searching through, like, a particular space and figuring out sort of what are the optimal actions to take.
sentences.zh: 例如，路径规划——假设你有一个……再次假设你在制作一个类 Rogue 游戏，你拥有这个网格世界，整个世界就是一个数字网格。

sentences.en: So, for example, path planning is, you know, let's say you have, again, let's say you're making a roguelike game and you have this grid world, you know, sort of like a, where the
sentences.zh: 你位于坐标 X，你在坐标 3, 5，然后你向左迈出一步，现在你位于坐标 4, 5。

sentences.en: whole world is just a grid of numbers.
sentences.zh: 非常离散，对吧？

sentences.en: You're at coordinate X, you're at, you're at, you know, coordinate 3, 5, and then you take a step to the left, now you're at coordinate 4, 5.
sentences.zh: 所以你想要在这个网格世界的某个迷宫中导航。

sentences.en: It's very discreet, right?
sentences.zh: 你想做的事就是进行规划。

sentences.en: And so, you know, you want to navigate through some maze in this grid world.
sentences.zh: 你想要尝试所有可能的移动方式，然后看看你处于什么位置。

sentences.en: What you want to do is to plan.
sentences.zh: 你离目标更近了吗？

sentences.en: You want to sort of try all the possible moves you can make and then see where you are.
sentences.zh: 还是离目标更远了？

sentences.en: Are you closer to the goal?
sentences.zh: 在我采取了这些不同的行动之后，世界的状态是怎样的？

sentences.en: Are you further away from the goal?
sentences.zh: 所以，回到 Lisp 的优势上来。

sentences.en: Like, what's the state of the world after, after these different actions I could take?
sentences.zh: 你可以创建一个哈希表，其键是整个世界，也就是当前世界的状态。

sentences.en: So, again, going back to LISP strengths, right?
sentences.zh: 在这个网格世界中，键可能就是你的位置，而值则是你距离目标有多近。

sentences.en: Okay, let's, you can create a hash table where the key is the entire world, the state of the world as it is.
sentences.zh: 或者甚至，你只想让哈希表以世界状态作为键，以“你是否见过这个状态”作为值。

sentences.en: So, in this grid world, the key might be just your position and the value would be, you know, how close you are to the goal.
sentences.zh: 如果我向左迈出一步，这是一个新状态。

sentences.en: Or maybe even just you want the hash table to store as a key the state of the world and as a value whether you've seen this state or not.
sentences.zh: 所以我会把它放进哈希表中。

sentences.en: So, if I take a step to the left, that's a new state.
sentences.zh: 然后，假设我尝试向右迈出一步。

sentences.en: So, I'll put that in the hash table.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这让我回到了出发时的状态。

sentences.en: And then, let's say I try taking a step to the right.
sentences.zh: 于是我查阅哈希表。

sentences.en: Well, that puts me in the same state I started at.
sentences.zh: 我说：嘿，这是我发现的新世界，我正处于坐标 4, 5 的世界。

sentences.en: So, I go to my hash table.
sentences.zh: 哈希表说：不，你以前来过这里。

sentences.en: I say, hey, here's some new world I discovered.
sentences.zh: 别费劲往前走了。

sentences.en: This is the world where I'm at coordinate 4, 5.
sentences.zh: 你在 4, 5 时已经尝试过所有的行动了。

sentences.en: And the hash table says, no, you've already been here before.
sentences.zh: 这样做能防止你陷入“左、右、左、右、左、右”的死循环中。

sentences.en: Like, don't bother trying to go further.
sentences.zh: 所以，最终你将探索完所有可能的游戏状态、所有的世界状态，直到你到达目标状态。

sentences.en: Like, you've already tried all the actions when you're at 4, 5.
sentences.zh: 进阶一点来说，哈希表不仅能记录你以前是否到过那个状态，还能记录你是如何到达那里的。

sentences.en: And so, doing this will keep you from just going left, right, left, right, left, right.
sentences.zh: 所以，一旦你到达了目标，你就可以说：好的，我访问过的或现在身处的这个世界状态，我是怎么来到这里的？

sentences.en: You know, so, eventually you'll explore all of the possible game states, all the possible world states until you get to the state where you're at the goal.
sentences.zh: 目标。

sentences.en: Now, to take it to the next level, the hash table could not only say whether you've been at that state before, but it could say how you got there.
sentences.zh: 状态

sentences.en: So, you know, once you get to the goal, you can say, okay, this state of the world that I visited or that I'm at now, how did I get here?
sentences.zh: 呢？

sentences.en: Check the hash table.
sentences.zh: 检查一下哈希表。

sentences.en: The hash table would say, oh, you got here by making a move to the right.
sentences.zh: 哈希表会告诉你，哦，你是通过向右移动到达这里的。

sentences.en: So, you could do the opposite, backtrack, right, make a move to the left and say, this state of the world, how did I get here?
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以反过来做，回溯，对吧，向左移动然后说，当前这个世界状态，我是怎么到这儿的？

sentences.en: And it could say, oh, you got here by moving down, so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 然后它会说，哦，你是通过向下移动到达这里的，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So, this is planning.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是规划。

sentences.en: And to do effective planning, you need good heuristics, which that's just simple algebra.
sentences.zh: 为了进行有效的规划，你需要好的启发式方法，而这其实就是简单的代数。

sentences.en: So, you can do heuristics in any language.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以在任何语言中使用启发式方法。

sentences.en: But you need an awesome hash table, and Lisp definitely gives you that.
sentences.zh: 但你需要一个极棒的哈希表，而Lisp绝对能给你提供这一点。

sentences.en: So, it's very useful for planning.
sentences.zh: 因此，它非常适合用于规划。

sentences.en: Expert systems, it was also good at this.
sentences.zh: 专家系统，它也很擅长这个。

sentences.en: This is kind of a buzzword.
sentences.zh: 这算是一个流行词吧。

sentences.en: Expert systems is basically planning, but instead of planning over something very discreet, like as we mentioned, planning through a grid world or something like that.
sentences.zh: 专家系统基本上就是规划，只不过不是针对非常离散的东西进行规划，就像我们提到的那样，在网格世界之类的环境中进行规划。

sentences.en: In the case of expert systems, you're planning over rules.
sentences.zh: 在专家系统的情况下，你是在规则的基础上进行规划。

sentences.en: So, this is similar to Prologue.
sentences.zh: 所以，这类似于Prolog语言。

sentences.en: Actually, this is almost exactly Prologue, but at a lower level, yeah.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这几乎就是Prolog，只不过是在一个较低的层面上，是的。

sentences.en: So, in the case of Prologue, it's this really high-level abstract language where you're specifying these rules.
sentences.zh: 所以，在Prolog的情况下，它是一种非常高级的抽象语言，你在其中指定这些规则。

sentences.en: In the case of Lisp, sort of, you would be creating the Prologue interpreter, essentially, in Lisp.
sentences.zh: 而在Lisp的情况下，某种程度上，你基本上是用Lisp来创建Prolog解释器。

sentences.en: But you could also do other low-level things, like you could have rules that were mathematically based.
sentences.zh: 但你也可以做其他底层的事情，比如你可以拥有基于数学的规则。

sentences.en: You do things like that.
sentences.zh: 你可以做类似的事情。

sentences.en: And so, a mathematically-based rule system, which parsed natural language, it basically tokenized the languages, the natural, tokenized the text into syllables.
sentences.zh: 所以，一个基于数学的规则系统，它解析自然语言，基本上是将语言分词，将自然语言文本分词成音节。

sentences.en: And then, based on the syllables, tried to get an understanding for the language, like where the noun is in the sentence, where the verb is.
sentences.zh: 然后，根据音节，试图理解语言，比如句子中的名词在哪里，动词在哪里。

sentences.en: There's a system that did this called SHRDLU, S-H-R-D-L-U.
sentences.zh: 有一个系统就是这样做的，叫做SHRDLU，S-H-R-D-L-U。

sentences.en: And it really made Lisp famous.
sentences.zh: 它真的让Lisp成名了。

sentences.en: So, what this guy did, he was able to scan an entire encyclopedia.
sentences.zh: 所以，这家伙做的事是，他能够扫描整部百科全书。

sentences.en: And then, for each sentence, he was able to figure out where the noun, the verb, the object of the preposition, all the different parts of speech for that sentence.
sentences.zh: 然后，对于每个句子，他都能够找出名词、动词、介词宾语，以及该句子的所有不同词性。

sentences.en: And then, he created a hash table for each sentence, where the key was the, I believe the key was the verb, and the value was the noun, something like that.
sentences.zh: 接着，他为每个句子创建一个哈希表，其中键是，我相信键是动词，值是名词，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But basically, because he scanned the entire encyclopedia, you could ask it questions, like, how many toes, or how many legs does a zebra have?
sentences.zh: 但基本上，因为他扫描了整部百科全书，你可以向它提问，比如，斑马有多少个脚趾，或者有多少条腿？

sentences.en: And it actually could tell you answers in English.
sentences.zh: 它实际上能用英文回答你。

sentences.zh: 所以你只需要字面输入：斑马有多少条腿？

sentences.zh: 它就会用英文回答你：斑马有四条腿。

sentences.en: So, you know, algebra really is a planning problem, you know, especially at a higher level.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，代数确实是一个规划问题，特别是在更高的层面上。

sentences.en: Like, you think about it, you have an equation.
sentences.zh: 比如，你想想，你有一个方程式。

sentences.en: Let's say you have, like, let's say a simple equation.
sentences.zh: 假设你有一个，比方说一个简单的方程式。

sentences.en: Like, you have, you know, 4 divided by 2 plus 3.
sentences.zh: 比如，你知道的，4除以2加3。

sentences.en: And you just want to know the answer to that.
sentences.zh: 你只是想知道这个问题的答案。

sentences.en: So, you know, that's, you're doing, you have to do planning.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这就是，你正在做，你必须进行规划。

sentences.en: And in this case, you only have one thing you can do, which is a division because of order of operations.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，你只有一件事可以做，那就是根据运算顺序进行除法。

sentences.en: So you divide the 4 by the 2.
sentences.zh: 所以你用4除以2。

sentences.en: That's your one action.
sentences.zh: 这就是你的一个动作。

sentences.en: Now you're into a new state where you have 2 plus 3.
sentences.zh: 现在你进入了一个新状态，你有2加3。

sentences.en: Then you take another action where you combine those and you get 5.
sentences.zh: 然后你采取另一个行动，将它们组合起来得到5。

sentences.en: But as you get to more advanced things, especially like integrals where there's many different rules you can use or derivatives.
sentences.zh: 但随着你接触到更高级的内容，尤其是像积分（有许多不同的规则可以使用）或导数。

sentences.en: Or you get to differential equations where there's, you know, 10, if not 15 or 20 different ways you can solve a particular ODE, particular differential equation.
sentences.zh: 或者当你接触到微分方程时，你知道，解决特定的常微分方程（ODE）有10种，甚至15种或20种不同的方法。

sentences.en: So, this thing does planning and says, all right, again, let's, here's the state of the world.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个东西会进行规划并说：好的，再次强调，这是当前的世界状态。

sentences.en: It's this differential equation.
sentences.zh: 它是这个微分方程。

sentences.en: Let's put it in a hash table.
sentences.zh: 让我们把它放进哈希表里。

sentences.en: And then let's start trying different rules, different ODE, different differential equation solvers.
sentences.zh: 然后让我们开始尝试不同的规则、不同的常微分方程求解器。

sentences.en: And it can, it can sort of try these rules.
sentences.zh: 它能够，它能够尝试这些规则。

sentences.en: And by enacting these rules on the equation, it creates a new equation.
sentences.zh: 通过对方程式实施这些规则，它创造了一个新的方程式。

sentences.en: And that's a new entry in the hash table.
sentences.zh: 这就是哈希表中的一个新条目。

sentences.en: And the hope is eventually it can reduce some really complex differential equation to something much simpler.
sentences.zh: 人们希望最终它能把一些非常复杂的微分方程简化为简单的形式。

sentences.en: Or it can reduce some integral using some trig identity into something much simpler.
sentences.zh: 或者它可以使用某种三角恒等式将某些积分化简为更简单的形式。

sentences.en: So, Maxima used planning to solve many computer algebra probleMs.
